Problem: Write a python function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.

Tests:
assert check_last([5,7,10],3,1) == "ODD"
assert check_last([2,3],2,3) == "EVEN"
assert check_last([1,2,3],3,1) == "ODD"

Write the t task named `check_last` with 3 parameter(s) of type(s) seq, int, int, in the order the tests pass them, returning seq. The tests must pass and the ensures must specify the result.

Let me just implement: add val to the last element p times, check if result is even or odd.

```t
t 0
task check_last(arr: seq, p: int, val: int) returns (r: seq)
  ensures r == "EVEN" or r == "ODD"
  ensures len(arr) > 0
  ensures (arr[len(arr) - 1] + p * val) % 2 == 0 ==> r == "EVEN"
  ensures (arr[len(arr) - 1] + p * val) % 2 == 1 ==> r == "ODD"
{
  var last: int := arr[len(arr) - 1] + p * val;
  if last % 2 == 0 {
    r := "EVEN";
  } else {
    r := "ODD";
  }
}
```

{
}

No, no division either. I need to check parity without modulo or division. I can use a loop or a recursive spec fun.

Let me use a helper to check evenness:

```t

gate loops
task check_last(arr: seq, p: int, val: int) returns (r: seq)
  requires len(arr) > 0
  ensures r == "EVEN" or r == "ODD"
  ensures is_even(arr[len(arr) - 1] + p * val) ==> r == "EVEN"
  ensures not is_even(arr[len(arr) - 1] + p * val) ==> r == "ODD"
spec fun is_even(n: int): bool
  decreases 0
= if n >= 0 then n == 0 or is_even(n - 2) else is_even(n + 2)
{

  }
}
```
